1.1 site type

  • Child of: Konzepte
  • Set of categories to characterise the use of a site by humans or its geological relevance.

  • Other Properties:

1.1.1 anthropogenic site

  • Child of: site type
  • The site is characterised by traces of human activity without any further specification.

  • Other Properties:

1.2.10.2 secondary ore

  • Child of: ore
  • The material that is extracted from a mineralisation because of its economic value that was altered by hydrothermal processes or weathering. The term usually refers to ore that became enriched in the targeted elements because of alteration processes.

  • Other Properties:

1.2.10.3 alteration

  • Child of: ore
  • The part of the ore that is affected by natural post-genetic processes, often including interaction with a hydrous fluid.

1.2.10.4.2 minor mineral

1.3.3 borehole survey

  • Child of: discovery activity
  • Drilling into the ground with the aim to collect samples and/or to describe the stratigraphy and subsurface features of archaeological and geological features.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_eb09b8cd
  • Other Properties:

1.3.3.1 core drilling

  • Child of: borehole survey
  • Drilling into the ground with the aim to retrieve the content of the borehole as a whole. The material will subsequently be used to collect samples and/or to describe the stratigraphy and subsurface features of archaeological and geological features.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_410a0d02
  • Other Properties:

1.3.3.2 auger drilling

  • Child of: borehole survey
  • Drilling into the ground with the aim to retrieve the content of the borehole as loose material to retrieve samples. In some cases, it can be used to infer stratigraphy and subsurface features of archaeological and geological features.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_19639bab
  • Other Properties:

1.3.4 metal detecting

  • Child of: discovery activity
  • The use of a metal detector to discover artefacts.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_3f471934

  • Child of: discovery activity
  • Controlled and documented intrusive fieldwork with the aim to record an site and to retrieve samples and artefacts from the site.

  • Other Properties:

1.3.5.1 research excavation

  • Child of: excavation
  • Controlled and documented intrusive fieldwork with the aim to answer a specific research question by recording an site and retrieving samples and artefacts from the site.

  • Other Properties:

1.3.5.2 rescue excavation

  • Child of: excavation
  • Controlled and documented intrusive fieldwork with the aim to record an site under threat of destruction and to retrieve samples and artefacts from the site under strict time constraints.

  • Other Properties:

1.3.5.3 underwater excavation

  • Child of: excavation
  • Controlled and documented intrusive fieldwork with the aim to record an underwater site and to retrieve samples and artefacts from the site.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_6a6e0a7f
  • Other Properties:

1.3.6 survey

  • Child of: discovery activity
  • Non-intrusive fieldwork to document the extent and layout of a site through recording the position and distribution of specimens and artefacts.

  • Other Properties:

1.3.7 mining

  • A cabinet with at least one transparent part specifically designed to present objects to a visitor, e.g. in a museum exhibition.

1.6 object life cycle stage

  • Child of: Konzepte
  • The different stages an object undergoes after its collection in the field.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_6eeee275
  • Other Properties:

1.6.1 storage stage

  • Child of: human interactions object life cycle stage
  • The object is stored in a place to keep it safe in the long term.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_20b5f585
  • Other Properties:

1.6.2 restoration stage

  • Child of: human interactions object life cycle stage
  • The object is brought back to its original shape as much as possible, often with addition of missing parts.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_084b00a4
  • Other Properties:

1.6.3 conservation stage

  • Child of: human interactions object life cycle stage
  • The object is treated in a conservation laboratory to stop ongoing deterioation and to prepare it for long-term storage.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_5282dab3
  • Other Properties:

1.6.4 finds processing stage

  • Child of: human interactions object life cycle stage
  • The object undergoes limited treatment in the field such as washing or basic convservation measures.
  • Alternate labels: in-situ conservation
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_75b32326
  • Other Properties:

1.6.5 discovery stage

  • Child of: human interactions object life cycle stage
  • The object did not received any treatment (yet) since its discovery.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_687c5f00
  • Other Properties:

1.6.6 laboratory stage

  • Child of: environnement bâti object life cycle stage
  • The object is under investigation in a laboratory.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_33bebd59

1.9.2.1 gossan

  • Child of: υλικά μορφώματα assemblage geological material

1.9.2.2 host rock

  • Child of: materials assemblage geological material gangue
  • The country rock or rock body in which a mineralisation occurs.

1.9.2.3 ore

  • Child of: materials assemblage geological material
  • The material that is extracted from a mineralisation because of its economic value.

1.9.2.3.1 primary ore

1.9.2.3.2 secondary ore
  • Child of: ore
  • The material that is extracted from a mineralisation because of its economic value that was altered by hydrothermal processes or weathering. The term usually refers to ore that became enriched in the targeted elements because of alteration processes.

1.9.2.3.3 alteration
  • Child of: ore

1.9.2.3.4.1 major mineral

1.9.2.3.4.2 minor mineral

1.9.2.4 wall rock

  • Child of: materials assemblage geological material

  • A usually small, flat and round piece of metal primarily used as medium of exchange or legal tender. It usually follows a standardised system in weight and sometimes size and is produced in large quantities.

1.10.3 in-situ

  • Child of: sample type

  • Child of: sample type

1.10.5 hand-picked

  • Child of: sample type
  • A part of the object was crushed and the sample manually separated after visual inspection of each fragment.

  • Other Properties:

1.10.6 mineral separate

  • Child of: sample type
  • A part of the object was crushed and the sample extracted based on its physical or chemical properties (e.g., density, magnetic properties).
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_0118bbdc
  • Other Properties:

1.10.7 leachate

  • Child of: sample type
  • Acids or other solvents were applied to a usually crushed part of the object to extract the sample as solution. Usually only done with geological material.

  • Other Properties:

1.10.8 swabbed material

  • Child of: sample type
  • Acids or other solvents are applied with a soft and absorbent tool (e.g., Q-tip, sponge) on the object to extract the sample as solution absorbed to the same tool and/or particles adhering to it. Usually only carried out on archaeological materials.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_07f899ac
  • Other Properties:

1.10.9 hand specimen fragments

  • Child of: sample type
  • The object was crushed in to pieces, which were then taken as sample. This is usually only done with larger items of geological origin such as rocks.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_d8e9f67e
  • Other Properties:

1.10.10 loose material

  • Child of: sample type
  • The object already had detached pieces, which were collected as sample.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_d57dc599
  • Other Properties:

1.10.11 cut

  • Child of: sample type
  • The sample is cut from the object with e.g. a blade or saw.

  • Other Properties:

1.10.12 section

  • Child of: sample type
  • A larger piece of the object is cut with the aim to create a section of it, usually for inspection with a microscope and/or if the object is too large to fit into the analytical instrument’s sample chamber.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_fb91df68
  • Other Properties:

1.10.12.1 polished section

  • Child of: section

  • Child of: sampling method

1.11.9.3 hand-picking

  • Child of: separation

  • Child of: méthodes
  • Procedures that operate on material samples to produce observation results with information about the physical properties, chemical or isotopic composition, crystallography, or molecular structure of the sample.

1.14.1 mass spectrometer

  • Child of: analytical method

1.14.1.1 TIMS

  • Child of: mass spectrometer
  • Mass spectrometer in which the sample is placed on a filament and ionised by heating the filament. With respect to lead isotope analyses, mass detection by a detector array in implied.

  • Other Properties:

1.14.1.2 ICP-MS

  • Child of: mass spectrometer
  • Mass spectrometry technique in which the sample is introduced into an inductively coupled plasma to atomize and ionize the sample for inlet to mass analyzer.

  • Other Properties:

1.14.1.2.1 MC-ICP-MS
  • Child of: ICP-MS

1.15 mass bias correction

  • Child of: méthodes
  • The mathematical model or procedure used to correct for the fractionation of an isotope ratio during measurement.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_5f1716a4
  • Other Properties:

1.15.1 linear model

  • Child of: mass bias correction
  • A mathematical model assuming a linear relationship between the isotope ratio of the sample and a different isotope ratio of an internal standard added to the sample.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_39d3b302
  • Other Properties:

1.15.2 double-spike

  • Child of: mass bias correction
  • The correction of an isotope ratio’s mass bias by altering the abundance of two other isotopes of the same element through the addition of an enriched isotopic spike
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_7b213d83
  • Other Properties:

1.15.3 standard-sample bracketing

  • Child of: mass bias correction
  • The correction of an isotope ratio’s mass bias in a sample by extrapolation from measurements of the same isotope ratio in an external standard measured before and after the sample.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_725495a8
  • Other Properties:

1.15.4 power law

  • Child of: mass bias correction
  • A mathematical model assuming a power-relationship between the isotope ratio of the sample and a different isotope ratio of an internal standard added to the sample.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_17be86eb
  • Other Properties:

1.15.5 exponential law

  • Child of: mass bias correction
  • A mathematical model assuming an exponential relationship between the isotope ratio of the sample and a different isotope ratio of an internal standard added to the sample.
  • Alternate labels: Russell model
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_e9b3f7f1
  • Other Properties:

1.16 reference material

  • Child of: materials
  • A reference material (RM) is a material that is sufficiently stable and homogeneous in one or more of its properties and whose use for the calibration of measurements has been established. A certified reference material (CRM) is characterised by metrologically valid procedures for one or more specified properties and is accompanied by a certificate for this characterisation. Standard reference material” (SRM) is a trademarked term for CRMs satisfying additional criteria specified by the United States National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST).
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_c7d45a2d

1.30 contributorType

  • Child of: roles of individuals
  • The type of contributor of the resource.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_e4ed600b
  • Other Properties:

1.30.1 Other (contributorType)

  • Child of: contributorType
  • Any person or institution making a significant contribution to the development and/or maintenance of the resource, but whose contribution is not adequately described by any of the other values for contributorType.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_3a208ae6
  • Other Properties:

1.30.2 WorkPackageLeader

  • Child of: contributorType
  • A Work Package is a recognized data product, not all of which is included in publication. The package, instead, may include notes, discarded documents, etc. The Work Package Leader is responsible for ensuring the comprehensive contents, versioning, and availability of the Work Package during the development of the resource.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_50da8fc6
  • Other Properties:

1.30.3 Translator

  • Child of: contributorType
  • A person, organization, or automated system responsible for converting the content of a resource from one language into another, preserving its meaning and intended message.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_79574dab
  • Other Properties:

1.30.4 Supervisor

  • Child of: contributorType
  • Designated administrator over one or more groups/teams working to produce a resource, or over one or more steps of a development process.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_2f9a64df
  • Other Properties:

1.30.5 Sponsor

  • Child of: contributorType
  • Person or organisation that issued a contract or under the auspices of which a work has been written, printed, published, developed, etc.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_8ff2aeb0
  • Other Properties:

1.30.6 RightsHolder

  • Child of: contributorType
  • Person or institution owning or managing property rights, including intellectual property rights over the resource.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_f18d65a2
  • Other Properties:

1.30.7 ResearchGroup

  • Child of: contributorType
  • Typically refers to a group of individuals with a lab, department, or division that has a specifically defined focus of activity.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_57b3dd9a
  • Other Properties:

1.30.8 Researcher

  • Child of: contributorType
  • A person involved in analysing data or the results of an experiment or formal study. May indicate an intern or assistant to one of the authors who helped with research but who was not so “key” as to be listed as an author.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_e1f2cf05
  • Other Properties:

1.30.9 RelatedPerson

  • Child of: contributorType
  • A person without a specifically defined role in the development of the resource, but who is someone the author wishes to recognize.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_ad00bdad
  • Other Properties:

1.30.10 RegistrationAuthority

  • Child of: contributorType
  • A standards-setting body from which Registration Agencies obtain official recognition and guidance.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_ebc3e072
  • Other Properties:

1.30.11 RegistrationAgency

  • Child of: contributorType
  • Institution/organisation officially appointed by a Registration Authority to handle specific tasks within a defined area of responsibility.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_c8f80f6c
  • Other Properties:

1.30.12 ProjectMember

  • Child of: contributorType
  • Person on the membership list of a designated project/project team.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_c6bb8064
  • Other Properties:

1.30.13 ProjectManager

  • Child of: contributorType
  • Person officially designated as manager of a project. Project may consist of one or many project teams and sub-teams.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_384d11d1
  • Other Properties:

1.30.14 ProjectLeader

  • Child of: contributorType
  • Person officially designated as head of project team or sub- project team instrumental in the work necessary to development of the resource.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_dd32fd29
  • Other Properties:

1.30.15 Producer

  • Child of: contributorType
  • Typically, a person or organisation responsible for the artistry and form of a media product.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_7250b71d
  • Other Properties:

1.30.16 HostingInstitution

  • Child of: contributorType
  • Typically, the organisation allowing the resource to be available on the internet through the provision of its hardware/software/operating support.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_041e374c
  • Other Properties:

1.30.17 Editor

  • Child of: contributorType
  • A person who oversees the details related to the publication format of the resource.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_36d34fdb
  • Other Properties:

1.30.18 Distributor

  • Child of: contributorType
  • Institution tasked with responsibility to generate/disseminate copies of the resource in either electronic or print form.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_62875695
  • Other Properties:

1.30.19 DataManager

  • Child of: contributorType
  • Person (or organisation with a staff of data managers, such as a data centre) responsible for maintaining the finished resource.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_8034b473
  • Other Properties:

1.30.20 DataCurator

  • Child of: contributorType
  • Person tasked with reviewing, enhancing, cleaning, or standardizing metadata and the associated data submitted for storage, use, and maintenance within a data centre or repository.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_eed9b69e
  • Other Properties:

1.30.21 DataCollector

  • Child of: contributorType
  • Person/institution responsible for finding or gathering/collecting data under the guidelines of the author(s) or Principal Investigator (PI).
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_f5974a2b
  • Other Properties:

1.30.22 ContactPerson

  • Child of: contributorType
  • Person with knowledge of how to access, troubleshoot, or otherwise field issues related to the resource.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_34e78a4f
  • Other Properties:

1.31 sample access

  • General information about whether objects or materials are available for investigation.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_6de9e3f7
  • Other Properties:

1.31.1 unknown

  • Child of: site type discovery activity context type sample housing object material authenticity sample material sample type sampling method sample state reference material alteration extent production context recycling indicator corrosion extent glass component compound type compound origin pigment component alteration process sample access production process
  • The information is not available.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_3e4fdfbb
  • Other Properties:

1.31.2 accessible

  • Child of: sample access
  • The object or material is generally accessible for investigation.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_06c40941
  • Other Properties:

1.31.3 policy

  • Child of: sample access
  • The institution holding the object or material has a policy regulating access to objects and materials for investigation.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_b1cf95c1
  • Other Properties:

1.31.4 inaccessible

  • Child of: sample access
  • The object or material is not accessible for investigation or analysis in general.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_fba4dbc9
  • Other Properties:

1.31.5 destroyed

  • Child of: sample access
  • The object or material was completely destroyed (e.g., during analysis or in a destruction event) with records for this event being available.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_5df8720f
  • Other Properties:

1.31.6 lost

  • Child of: sample access
  • The object or material cannot be localised any more and its whereabouts cannot be reconstructed.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_6e9109c4
  • Other Properties:

1.32 date type

  • Child of: tipos de épocas
  • Whether a date refers to an archaeological or geological event or period.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_5592fbc1
  • Other Properties:

1.32.1 archaeological

  • Child of: date type
  • Adjective of “archaeology”, which refers to the study of the human past.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_ee0cd6f1
  • Other Properties:

1.32.2 geological

  • Child of: date type
  • Adjective of “geology”, which refers to the study of the Earth’s history, composition, structure, physical properties and relevant processes.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_de82ab14
  • Other Properties:

1.33 dating technique

  • Child of: méthodes
  • Determining the date of an event or in time or relatively to other other events.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_458c8d5b
  • Other Properties:

1.33.1 absolute dating

  • Child of: dating technique
  • Dating technique that results dates in calendar years.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_70421df0
  • Other Properties:

1.33.1.1 dendrochronology

  • Child of: absolute dating
  • The measurement of a sequence of tree growth rings and their relative differences in width and the comparison of this information to known reference curves.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_bf02bc84
  • Other Properties:

1.33.1.2 lichenometry

  • Child of: absolute dating
  • The measurement of lichens’ size on rock surfaces.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_e71424b2
  • Other Properties:

1.33.1.3 luminescence dating

  • Child of: absolute dating
  • The measurement of the released stored energy in a material in the form of light to determine the material’s age.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_14f0b363
  • Other Properties:

1.33.1.3.1 optically stimulated luminescence dating
  • Child of: luminescence dating
  • The measurement of the stored energy in a material in the form of light released by exposing the material to a strong light source (e.g. lamp or laser) to determine the material’s age.
  • Alternate labels: OSL
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_8d044281
  • Other Properties:

1.33.1.3.2 thermoluminescence dating
  • Child of: luminescence dating
  • The measurement of the stored energy in a material in the form of light released by heating the material to determine the material’s age.
  • Alternate labels: TL
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_8650222c
  • Other Properties:

1.33.1.4 radiometric dating

  • Child of: absolute dating
  • A family of dating methods that rely on the decay of radioactive isotopes.
  • Alternate labels: radioactive dating
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_3f00a8dc
  • Other Properties:

1.33.1.4.1 fission track dating
  • Child of: radiometric dating
  • Determining the age of a glassy material by counting the number of damage trails created through the radioactive decay of uranium atoms in the material.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_44573a53
  • Other Properties:

1.33.1.4.2 potassium-argon dating
  • Child of: radiometric dating
  • Determination of the age through the ratio of a radioactive potassium isotope and the argon isotope it decays into.
  • Alternate labels: K-Ar dating
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_ade3d830
  • Other Properties:

1.33.1.4.2.1 argon-argon dating
  • Child of: potassium-argon dating
  • A dating method superseding potassium-argon dating by allowing age determination from a single analysis. This is achieved by converting a controlled amount of the radioactive potassium isotope to a not naturally occurring argon isotope by neutron irradiation.
  • Alternate labels: Ar-Ar dating
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_025785fd
  • Other Properties:

1.33.1.4.3 uranium-series dating
  • Child of: radiometric dating
  • Determination of the age by determining the extent to which the secular equilibrium between 230Th and 234U was restored in a material that was nominally thorium-free at the point of its creation.
  • Alternate labels: U-series dating
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_f0e6044b
  • Other Properties:

1.33.1.4.4 radiocarbon dating
  • Child of: radiometric dating
  • Determination of the age through the remaining radioactivity of carbon 14 in biogenic materials.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_4b83987e
  • Other Properties:

1.33.1.4.5 uranium-lead dating
  • Child of: radiometric dating
  • Determination of the age through the two decay series of uranium isotopes to lead isotopes.
  • Alternate labels: U-Pb dating
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_acb27762
  • Other Properties:

1.33.1.4.6 rubidium-strontium dating
  • Child of: radiometric dating
  • Determination of the age through the ratio of a radioactive rubidium isotope and the strontium isotope it decays into.
  • Alternate labels: Rb-Sr dating
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_f21ed82d
  • Other Properties:

1.33.1.4.7 lutetium-hafnium dating
  • Child of: radiometric dating
  • Determination of the age through the ratio of a radioactive lutetium isotope and the hafnium isotope it decays into.
  • Alternate labels: Lu-Hf dating
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_5dec7fcf
  • Other Properties:

1.33.1.4.8 samarium-neodymium dating
  • Child of: radiometric dating
  • Determination of the age through the ratio of a radioactive samarium isotope and the neodymium isotope it decays into.
  • Alternate labels: Sm-Nd dating
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_c8c1af39
  • Other Properties:

1.33.1.4.9 rhenium-osmium dating
  • Child of: radiometric dating
  • Determination of the age through the ratio of a radioactive rhenium isotope and the osmium isotope it decays into.
  • Alternate labels: Rh-Os dating
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_eb290340
  • Other Properties:

1.33.1.4.10 lead-lead dating
  • Child of: radiometric dating
  • Determination of the age through the ratios of the the lead isotopes resulting from the radioactive decay of uranium and the stable lead isotope ratio.
  • Alternate labels: Pb-Pb dating
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_f98943fa
  • Other Properties:

1.33.1.5 rehydroxylation dating

  • Child of: absolute dating
  • The measurement of the hydroxyl content in fired clay and the determination of the related chemical kinetics to reconstruct the date of the material.
  • Alternate labels: RHX
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_e6861de4
  • Other Properties:

1.33.2 relative dating

  • Child of: dating technique
  • Dating technique that allows to put objects in a sequence relative to each other that cannot be tied to calendar years.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_25bf9b34
  • Other Properties:

1.33.2.1 seriation

  • Child of: relative dating
  • Recording the stylistic details of a group of items and ordering them in a sequence based defined typological features.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_e2a8665e
  • Other Properties:

1.33.2.2 archaeomagnetic dating

  • Child of: relative dating
  • The measurement of the direction and intensity of the magnetic information in materials and its comparison to known records of fluctuations in the magnetic field of the Earth. Archaeomagnetic dating refers to the dating of anthropogenic materials (e.g, fired clay), while palaeomagnetic dating refers to the dating of geogenic origin (e.g. rocks).
  • Alternate labels: palaeomagnetic dating
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_e1bf335f
  • Other Properties:

1.33.2.3 biostratigraphy

  • Child of: relative dating
  • The determination of the relative sequence of sediments or rocks based on the fossils found in them.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_b767c559
  • Other Properties:

1.33.2.4 tephrochronology

  • Child of: relative dating
  • The determination of the relative sequence of volcanic deposits (tephra), especially through studying their stratigraphy (tephra).
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_5ef3d79f
  • Other Properties:

1.34 analytical uncertainty

  • Child of: Konzepte
  • An expression for the statistical dispersion of a measured value.
  • Alternate labels: measurement uncertainty
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_6ae288a3
  • Other Properties:

1.34.1 standard error

  • Child of: analytical uncertainty
  • The standard error of the mean (SEM) is data item denoting the standard deviation of the sample-mean’s estimate of a population mean. It is calculated by dividing the sample standard deviation (i.e., the sample-based estimate of the standard deviation of the population) by the square root of n , the size (number of observations) of the sample. A measure of dispersion applied to means across hypothetical repeated random samples.
  • Alternate labels: SE
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_1c8f3d46
  • Other Properties:

1.34.2 standard deviation

  • Child of: analytical uncertainty
  • The standard deviation of a random variable, statistical population, data set, or probability distribution is a measure of variation which correspond to the average distance from the mean of the data set to any given point of that dataset. It also corresponds to the square root of its variance.
  • Alternate labels: SD
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_ed11712a
  • Other Properties:

1.35 identifier

  • Child of: objetos proposicionais
  • A string unique for a specific resource or feature.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_c8cb9106
  • Other Properties:

1.35.1 w3id

  • Child of: identifier
  • Mostly used to publish vocabularies and ontologies. The letters ‘w3’ stand for “World Wide Web”.
  • Alternate labels: Permanent identifier for Web applications
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_f260a576
  • Other Properties:

1.35.2 URN

  • Child of: identifier
  • A unique and persistent identifier of an electronic document. The syntax is: urn::. The leading urn: sequence is case- insensitive, is the namespace identifier, is the namespace-specific string.
  • Alternate labels: Uniform Resource Name
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_efbf8c56
  • Other Properties:

1.35.3 URL

  • Child of: identifier
  • Also known as web address, a URL is a specific character string that constitutes a reference to a resource. The syntax is: scheme://domain:port/path?query_string#fragment_id.
  • Alternate labels: Uniform Resource Locator
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_cca94dd2
  • Other Properties:

1.35.4 UPC

  • Child of: identifier
  • A barcode symbology used for tracking trade items in stores. Its most common form, the UPC-A, consists of 12 numerical digits.
  • Alternate labels: Universal Product Code
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_49ebd1fc
  • Other Properties:

1.35.5 SWHID

  • Child of: identifier
  • A unique and persistent identifier for software code artifacts commonly found in version control systems such as code files and commits available in the Software Heritage Archive. It consists of the mandatory identifier of the record in the Software Heritage archive and an optional list of qualifiers to provide information about the object’s context.
  • Alternate labels: SoftWare Hash Identifier
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_b573f515
  • Other Properties:

1.35.6 RRID

  • Child of: identifier
  • A character string used to uniquely identify key inputs to an experiment including the so-called “key biological resources” as defined by the National Institutes of Health, and related tools such as core facilities and databases. An RRID name is divided into two parts, the authority and a local identifier, separated by an underscore.
  • Alternate labels: Research Resource IDentifier
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_96a8c2b8
  • Other Properties:

1.35.7 RAiD

  • Child of: identifier
  • A unique and persistent identifier for research projects.
  • Alternate labels: Research Activity Identifier
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_b10276d1
  • Other Properties:

1.35.8 PURL

  • Child of: identifier
  • A PURL has three parts: (1) a protocol, (2) a resolver address, and
  1. a name.
  • Alternate labels: Persistent Uniform Resource Locator
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_ff6b1f44
  • Other Properties:

1.35.9 PMID

  • Child of: identifier
  • A unique number assigned to each PubMed record.
  • Alternate labels: PubMed identifier
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_491eec33
  • Other Properties:

1.35.10 LSID

  • Child of: identifier
  • A unique identifier for data in the Life Science domain. Format: urn:lsid:authority:namespace:identifier:revision.
  • Alternate labels: Life Science Identifiers
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_19665f86
  • Other Properties:

1.35.11 LISSN

  • Child of: identifier
  • Alternate labels: Linking ISSN
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_036b6cbe
  • Other Properties:

1.35.12 ISTC

  • Child of: identifier
  • A unique “number” assigned to a textual work. An ISTC consists of 16 numbers and/or letters.
  • Alternate labels: International Standard Text Code
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_a61ff4a5
  • Other Properties:

1.35.13 ISSN

  • Child of: identifier
  • A unique 8-digit number used to identify a print or electronic periodical publication.
  • Alternate labels: International Standard Serial Number
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_23aeb12c
  • Other Properties:

1.35.14 ISBN

  • Child of: identifier
  • A unique numeric book identifier. There are 2 formats: a 10-digit ISBN format and a 13-digit ISBN.
  • Alternate labels: International Standard Book Number
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_664844dc
  • Other Properties:

1.35.15 IGSN

  • Child of: identifier
  • A code that uniquely identifies samples from our natural environment and related features-of-interest.
  • Alternate labels: International Generic Sample Number
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_bb41a882
  • Other Properties:

1.35.16 Handle

  • Child of: identifier
  • This refers specifically to an ID in the Handle system operated by the Corporation for National Research Initiatives (CNRI).
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_db36371f
  • Other Properties:

1.35.17 EISSN

  • Child of: identifier
  • ISSN used to identify periodicals in electronic form (eISSN or e-ISSN).
  • Alternate labels: Electronic International Standard Serial Number
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_9cdedeb0
  • Other Properties:

1.35.18 EAN13

  • Child of: identifier
  • A 13-digit barcoding standard that is a superset of the original 12-digit Universal Product Code (UPC) system.
  • Alternate labels: European Article Number, International Article Number,
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_91caa317
  • Other Properties:

1.35.19 DOI

  • Child of: identifier
  • A character string used to uniquely identify an object. A DOI name is divided into two parts, a prefix and a suffix, separated by a slash.
  • Alternate labels: Digital Object Identifier
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_cc3c0083
  • Other Properties:

1.35.20 CSTR

  • Child of: identifier
  • CSTR is an identifier based on the Chinese National Standard GB/T 32843—2016 “Science and technology resource identification”, providing a unique identification service for scientific data, papers, scientific institutions, researchers, scientific instruments, patents and other scientific and technological resources.
  • Alternate labels: Common Science and Technology Resources Identifier
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_e3b9ba37
  • Other Properties:

1.35.21 bibcode

  • Child of: identifier
  • A standardized 19-character identifier according to the syntax yyyyjjjjjvvvvmppppa. See http://info-uri.info/registry/OAIHandler?verb =GetRecord&metadataPrefix=reg&identifier=info:bibcode/.
  • Alternate labels: Astrophysics Data System bibliographic codes
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_58ef12c9
  • Other Properties:

1.35.22 ArXiv

  • Child of: identifier
  • arXiv.org is a repository of preprints of scientific papers in the fields of mathematics, physics, astronomy, computer science, quantitative biology, statistics, and quantitative finance.
  • Alternate labels: arXiv identifier
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_14d152fa
  • Other Properties:

1.35.23 ARK

  • Child of: identifier
  • A URI designed to support long-term access to information objects. In general, ARK syntax is of the form (brackets, []. indicate optional elements): [http://NMA/]ark:/NAAN/Name [Qualifier].
  • Alternate labels: Archival Resource Key
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_9c7b1aa6
  • Other Properties:

1.36 relationType

  • Child of: Konzepte
  • Describes a relationship between the source being regstered (A) and the related source (B).
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_2c9da0f0
  • Other Properties:

1.36.1 HasTranslation

  • Child of: relationType
  • indicates A has a translation B
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_42798d88
  • Other Properties:

1.36.2 IsTranslationOf

  • Child of: relationType
  • indicates A is a translation of B
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_3e9a7d5d
  • Other Properties:

1.36.3 Collects

  • Child of: relationType
  • indicates A collects B
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_50f18eec
  • Other Properties:

1.36.4 IsCollectedBy

  • Child of: relationType
  • indicates A is collected by B
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_7209d768
  • Other Properties:

1.36.5 IsObsoletedBy

  • Child of: relationType
  • indicates A is replaced by B
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_b87ae52a
  • Other Properties:

1.36.6 Obsoletes

  • Child of: relationType
  • indicates A replaces B
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_a03285c1
  • Other Properties:

1.36.7 Requires

  • Child of: relationType
  • indicates A requires B
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_83af8ee5
  • Other Properties:

1.36.8 IsRequiredBy

  • Child of: relationType
  • indicates A is required by B
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_f0352501
  • Other Properties:

1.36.9 IsSourceOf

  • Child of: relationType
  • indicates A is a source upon which B is based
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_d7654681
  • Other Properties:

1.36.10 IsDerivedFrom

  • Child of: relationType
  • indicates B is a source upon which A is based
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_8aa44c44
  • Other Properties:

1.36.11 Reviews

  • Child of: relationType
  • indicates that A is a review of B
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_1565380d
  • Other Properties:

1.36.12 IsReviewedBy

  • Child of: relationType
  • indicates that A is reviewed by B
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_8941e0d4
  • Other Properties:

1.36.13 IsIdenticalTo

  • Child of: relationType
  • indicates that A is identical to B, for use when there is a need to register two separate instances of the same resource
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_58ed789b
  • Other Properties:

1.36.14 IsOriginalFormOf

  • Child of: relationType
  • indicates A is the original form of B
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_f214a28f
  • Other Properties:

1.36.15 IsVariantFormOf

  • Child of: relationType
  • indicates A is a variant or different form of B
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_4ccf0580
  • Other Properties:

1.36.16 Compiles

  • Child of: relationType
  • indicates B is the result of a compile or creation event using A
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_ad976a89
  • Other Properties:

1.36.17 IsCompiledBy

  • Child of: relationType
  • indicates B is used to compile or create A
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_38b56cad
  • Other Properties:

1.36.18 Documents

  • Child of: relationType
  • indicates A is documentation about/explaining B
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_85ea27dc
  • Other Properties:

1.36.19 IsDocumentedBy

  • Child of: relationType
  • indicates B is documentation about/explaining A
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_d85f7b3a
  • Other Properties:

1.36.20 References

  • Child of: relationType
  • indicates B is used as a source of information for A
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_9e3bfeb6
  • Other Properties:

1.36.21 IsReferencedBy

  • Child of: relationType
  • indicates A is used as a source of information by B
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_6510b31c
  • Other Properties:

1.36.22 IsPublishedIn

  • Child of: relationType
  • indicates A is published inside B, but is independent of other things published inside of B
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_50fb5931
  • Other Properties:

1.36.23 HasPart

  • Child of: relationType
  • indicates A includes the part B
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_99ef8f93
  • Other Properties:

1.36.24 IsPartOf

  • Child of: relationType
  • indicates A is a portion of B; may be used for elements of a series

1.39 resourceType

  • Child of: objetos proposicionais
  • The type of a resource.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_4f75cdd5
  • Other Properties:

1.39.1 Other (resourceType)

  • Child of: resourceType
  • Any resource not covered by other terms. If selected, provide resource type in metadata field “additional information”.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_e4111c25
  • Other Properties:

1.39.2 Workflow

  • Child of: resourceType
  • A structured series of steps which can be executed to produce a final outcome, allowing users a means to specify and enact their work in a more reproducible manner.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_eb3431d5
  • Other Properties:

1.39.3 Text

  • Child of: resourceType
  • A resource consisting primarily of words for reading that is not covered by any other textual resource type in this list.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_9fadd71a
  • Other Properties:

1.39.4 StudyRegistration

  • Child of: resourceType
  • A detailed, time-stamped description of a research plan, often openly shared in a registry or published in a journal before the study is conducted to lend accountability and transparency in the hypothesis generating and testing process.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_d9a7c870
  • Other Properties:

1.39.5 Standard

  • Child of: resourceType
  • Something established by authority, custom, or general consent as a model, example, or point of reference.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_2ac847b2
  • Other Properties:

1.39.6 Sound

  • Child of: resourceType
  • A resource primarily intended to be heard.
  • Alternate labels: Audio recording
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_c2b67ae7
  • Other Properties:

1.39.7 Software

  • Child of: resourceType
  • A computer program other than a computational notebook, in either source code (text) or compiled form. Use this type for general software components supporting scholarly research. Use the “ComputationalNotebook” value for virtual notebooks.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_b359ddc1
  • Other Properties:

1.39.8 Service

  • Child of: resourceType
  • An organized system of apparatus, appliances, staff, etc., for supplying some function(s) required by end users.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_40899a25
  • Other Properties:

1.39.9 Report

  • Child of: resourceType
  • A document that presents information in an organized format for a specific audience and purpose.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_21afb462
  • Other Properties:

1.39.10 Project

  • Child of: resourceType
  • A planned endeavor or activity, frequently collaborative, intended to achieve a particular aim using allocated resources such as budget, time, and expertise.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_78ce6c50
  • Other Properties:

1.39.11 Preprint

  • Child of: resourceType
  • A version of a scholarly or scientific paper that precedes formal peer review and publication in a peer-reviewed scholarly or scientific journal.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_945645e4
  • Other Properties:

1.39.12 PhysicalObject

  • Child of: resourceType
  • A physical object or substance.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_1e1210c6
  • Other Properties:

1.39.13 PeerReview

  • Child of: resourceType
  • Evaluation of scientific, academic, or professional work by others working in the same field.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_192f8727
  • Other Properties:

1.39.14 OutputManagementPlan

  • Child of: resourceType
  • A formal document that outlines how research outputs are to be handled both during a research project and after the project is completed.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_c5e4fd1c
  • Other Properties:

1.39.15 Model

  • Child of: resourceType
  • An abstract, conceptual, graphical, mathematical or visualization model that represents empirical objects, phenomena, or physical processes.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_095c193d
  • Other Properties:

1.39.16 JournalArticle

  • Child of: resourceType
  • A written composition on a topic of interest, which forms a separate part of a journal.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_b0ef03ef
  • Other Properties:

1.39.17 Journal

  • Child of: resourceType
  • A scholarly publication consisting of articles that is published regularly throughout the year.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_15f86bc5
  • Other Properties:

1.39.18 InteractiveResource

  • Child of: resourceType
  • A resource requiring interaction from the user to be understood, executed, or experienced.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_6d0e1459
  • Other Properties:

1.39.19 Instrument

  • Child of: resourceType
  • A device, tool or apparatus used to obtain, measure and/or analyze data.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_d40d5def
  • Other Properties:

1.39.20 Image

  • Child of: resourceType
  • A visual representation other than text.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_d16e61fe
  • Other Properties:

  • Child of: resourceType
  • A non-persistent, time-based occurrence.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_4229295c
  • Other Properties:

1.39.22 Dissertation

  • Child of: resourceType
  • A written essay, treatise, or thesis, especially one written by a candidate for the degree of Doctor of Philosophy.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_3839e9ab
  • Other Properties:

1.39.23 Dataset

  • Child of: resourceType

  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_985fe775
  • Other Properties:

1.39.24 DataPaper

  • Child of: resourceType
  • A factual and objective publication with a focused intent to identify and describe specific data, sets of data, or data collections to facilitate discoverability.

  • Other Properties:

1.39.25 ConferenceProceeding

  • Child of: resourceType
  • Collection of academic papers published in the context of an academic conference.

  • Other Properties:

1.39.26 ConferencePaper

  • Child of: resourceType

  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_afd22872
  • Other Properties:

1.39.27 ComputationalNotebook

  • Child of: resourceType

  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_0afde725
  • Other Properties:

1.39.28 Collection

  • Child of: resourceType
  • An aggregation of resources, which may encompass collections of one resourceType as well as those of mixed types. A collection is described as a group; its parts may also be separately described.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_76209e5e
  • Other Properties:

1.39.29 BookChapter

  • Child of: resourceType
  • One of the main divisions of a book.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_fc66bc62
  • Other Properties:

1.39.30 Book

  • Child of: resourceType
  • A medium for recording information in the form of writing or images, typically composed of many pages bound together and protected by a cover.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_5c0c5449
  • Other Properties:

1.39.31 Award

  • Child of: resourceType
  • An umbrella term for resources provided to individual(s) or organization(s) in support of research, academic output, or training, such as a specific instance of funding, grant, investment, sponsorship, scholarship, recognition, or non-monetary materials.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_a8c92376
  • Other Properties:

1.39.32 Audiovisual

  • Child of: resourceType
  • A series of visual representations imparting an impression of motion when shown in succession. May or may not include sound.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_30709214
  • Other Properties:

1.40 registry

  • Child of: objetos proposicionais

  • Other Properties:

1.40.1 gazetteer

  • Child of: registry

1.40.1.1 WHG

  • Child of: gazetteer
  • The World History Gazetteer provides authoritative data for historic and archaeological sites for the entire globe.

  • Other Properties:

1.40.1.2 TGN

  • Child of: gazetteer
  • The Getty Thesaurus of Geographic Names is a structured vocabulary for places important in arts and architecture.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_2c0d9965
  • Other Properties:

1.40.1.3 Geonames

  • Child of: gazetteer

  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_c18450b7
  • Other Properties:

1.40.1.4 Pleiades

  • Child of: gazetteer
  • Pleiades is a community-built gazetteer for archaeological and historical sites with focus on the ancient Mediterrean and neighbouring regions.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_81d9c666
  • Other Properties:

1.40.1.5 iDAI.gazetteer

  • Child of: gazetteer
  • The gazetteer of the German Archaeological Institute.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_eb965d6a
  • Other Properties:

1.40.1.6 PeriodO

  • Child of: gazetteer
  • PeriodO is a gazetteer for chronological information of archaeological, historical and art-historical periods.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_d012defe
  • Other Properties:

1.40.2 GND

  • Child of: registry
  • The Gemeinsame Normdatei (GND, Integrated Authority File) of the German National Library provides authoritative data on a wide range of topics, among them persons, corporate bodies and geographic entities. Its main target groups are libraries who used it for cataloguing their publication.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_ef46e5df
  • Other Properties:

1.40.3 ORCID

  • Child of: registry
  • The Open Researcher and Contributor ID organization offers persistent identifiers of the same name for persons, with researchers and scholars as their main audience.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_c62b90a7
  • Other Properties:

1.40.4 iDAI ChronOntology

  • Child of: registry
  • ChronOntology is the ontology for chronological information of the German Archaological Institute.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_fb11b880
  • Other Properties:

1.42 mineral texture

  • Child of: υλικά μορφώματα
  • The relationship between the mineral and the matrix and other minerals, conveying information about the mineral’s formation conditions.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_8441accd
  • Other Properties:

1.42.1 intergrowth

  • Child of: mineral texture
  • The state of interlocking of different mineral grains due to simultaneous crystallisation.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_e74b28a0
  • Other Properties:

1.42.1.1 ophitic

  • Child of: intergrowth
  • Large and often lath-shaped euhedral or subhedral crystals are partly or fully included in much larger crystals.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_dd1113d4
  • Other Properties:

1.42.1.2 intersertal

  • Child of: intergrowth
  • Filling of interstitial space with a glass or a vitreous phase with small crystals.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_cab80d83
  • Other Properties:

1.42.1.3 interstitial

  • Child of: intergrowth
  • The mineral grew in the interstitial space between grains or structures.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_1a4f781a
  • Other Properties:

1.42.1.4 interlocked

  • Child of: intergrowth
  • Intimate intergrowth of randomly orientated mineral grains with no gaps or cement between them.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_3e50acb7
  • Other Properties:

1.42.1.5 symplectitic

  • Child of: intergrowth
  • The fine-grained vermicular (“worm-shaped”) intergrowth of two minerals, often indicating the breakdown of unstable phases.
  • Alternate labels: vermicular
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_9e0d2c4a
  • Other Properties:

1.42.1.5.1 myrmekitic
  • Child of: symplectitic
  • A symplectitic intergrowth of plagioclase and vermicular quartz.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_5eaf970c
  • Other Properties:

1.42.1.6 poikiloblastic

  • Child of: intergrowth
  • Small grains of one mineral are randomly scattered without common orientation in larger grains of another mineral.
  • Alternate labels: poikilitic, sieve texture,
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_6655861f
  • Other Properties:

1.42.1.7 disseminated

  • Child of: intergrowth
  • The mineral is scattered as small grains throughout another mineral or the matrix.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_aa5d33c3
  • Other Properties:

1.42.1.8 rimmed

  • Child of: intergrowth
  • A mineral grew in the rim of another mineral.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_436d944e
  • Other Properties:

1.42.1.9 amoeboid

  • Child of: intergrowth
  • A mineral with irregular outlines and anhedral crystals.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_e5b6f80a
  • Other Properties:

1.42.1.10 cellular (intergrowth)

  • Child of: intergrowth
  • Growth of minerals in small roughly regular-shaped rounded aggregates that resemble the shape of biological cells. Or the porous texture of a rock characterised by abundant openings or cavities, which may or may not be connected.
  • Alternate labels: porous, cavernous, vesicular,
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_04619e43
  • Other Properties:

1.42.1.11 atoll-like

  • Child of: intergrowth
  • The growth of a ring-shaped mineral around and surrounded by other minerals.
  • Alternate labels: core texture
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_95b262b5
  • Other Properties:

1.42.2 replacement

  • Child of: mineral texture
  • The growth of a new or chemically different mineral as a reaction product of the already existing mineral.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_a3d375e7
  • Other Properties:

1.42.2.1 filiform

  • Child of: replacement
  • An intergrowth of different minerals in which the larger crystals have a fairly regular geometric outline and orientation, and resemble cuneiform writing or have a thread-like appearance.
  • Alternate labels: graphic texture
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_f478f111
  • Other Properties:

1.42.2.2 graphic

  • Child of: replacement
  • The growth of elongated rounded aggregates of secondary minerals inside the primary mineral, often as a result of alteration of the primary mineral.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_52eaf264
  • Other Properties:

1.42.2.3 cellular (replacement)

  • Child of: replacement
  • The growth of minerals replacing the content of cells in originally biological matter such as plants in coal.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_8c47dce3
  • Other Properties:

1.42.2.4 island-shaped

  • Child of: replacement
  • The original mineral reacted from the outside, leaving an (island- shaped) unreacted part surrounded by secondary minerals.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_7b190793
  • Other Properties:

1.42.2.5 boxwork

  • Child of: replacement
  • Growth of secondary minerals in cavities and along fracture or cleavage planes from which previously present minerals were removed by e.g. dissolution, creating a network texture resembling stacked boxes or honey-combs.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_d78ab7be
  • Other Properties:

1.42.2.6 skeleton-shaped

  • Child of: replacement
  • Relict of a skeletal crystal of one mineral enclosed in another mineral species.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_36ca06ef
  • Other Properties:

1.42.2.7 cusp-and-caries

  • Child of: replacement
  • The growth of a secondary mineral from the grain boundary into the primary minerals, resulting in a grain boundary between both minerals with many scallop-shaped, concave embayments.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_d3b9f898
  • Other Properties:

1.42.2.8 lacuna

  • Child of: replacement
  • The dissolution of small areas of a mineral, often at its rim, resulting in voids.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_bb44a01a
  • Other Properties:

1.42.2.9 lamellar

  • Child of: replacement
  • The oriented growth of a secondary mineral in elongated shapes within the primary mineral, usually along cleavage planes, crystal planes, twin boundaries or fractures.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_7fe5c1ff
  • Other Properties:

1.42.2.10 zonal

  • Child of: replacement
  • The evenly-spaced growth of a secondary mineral along the crystallographic orientation of the primary mineral’s grain boundary.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_7d8b3c14
  • Other Properties:

1.42.2.11 atoll-like (replacement)

  • Child of: replacement
  • The replacement of one mineral by another with leaving the outermost original mineral unaffected, and constituting the “atoll”.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_dd91efb2
  • Other Properties:

1.42.2.12 cement-shaped

  • Child of: replacement
  • The growth of a dense anhedral alteration mineral in the matrix.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_d375a5c9
  • Other Properties:

1.42.2.13 pseudomorph

  • Child of: replacement
  • A secondary mineral completely replacing the primary mineral while retaining the shape of the primary mineral’s grains.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_0571a899
  • Other Properties:

1.42.3 deformation-related

  • Child of: mineral texture
  • The alteration of minerals through external mechanical stress.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_88091e76
  • Other Properties:

1.42.3.1 cataclastic

  • Child of: deformation-related
  • The fracturing of a mineral due to intense mechanical stress.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_6783bb4e
  • Other Properties:

1.42.3.2 brecciated

  • Child of: deformation-related
  • The fragmentation of a mineral resulting in various angular fragments
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_430fd693
  • Other Properties:

1.42.3.3 broken

  • Child of: deformation-related
  • The fragmentation of a mineral.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_03b13243
  • Other Properties:

1.42.3.4 translation lamellae

  • Child of: deformation-related
  • The internal deformation of a mineral’s crystal due to translational forces, resulting in the re-orientation of some areas in the crystal along crystal planes unrelated to the crystallographic axes
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_3136dfed
  • Other Properties:

1.42.3.5 pressure twins

  • Child of: deformation-related
  • The internal deformation of a mineral’s crystal due to translational forces, resulting in the re-orientation of some areas in the crystal along crystal planes along its crystallographic axes.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_7067812d
  • Other Properties:

1.42.3.6 bending

  • Child of: deformation-related
  • The ductile transformation of a mineral into a bent shape (i.e., without breaking it).
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_c8069a37
  • Other Properties:

1.42.3.7 planar alignment

  • Child of: deformation-related
  • The transformation of elongated or layered minerals into a (sub)parallel orientation.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_ed4b7838
  • Other Properties:

1.45 production process

  • The process by which a material was modified as part of the production process.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_25f0249a
  • Other Properties:

1.45.1 unknown

  • Child of: site type discovery activity context type sample housing object material authenticity sample material sample type sampling method sample state reference material alteration extent production context recycling indicator corrosion extent glass component compound type compound origin pigment component alteration process sample access production process
  • The information is not available.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_3e4fdfbb
  • Other Properties:

1.45.2 other

  • Child of: object material reference material analytical instrument alteration process production process
  • Any material, type or term not covered by other terms.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_ebc979f8
  • Other Properties:

1.45.3 absorption

  • Child of: production process
  • The material is exposed to another material from which a specific compound or the entire material gets dissolved into the material.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_31f5fc72
  • Other Properties:

1.45.4 weathering

  • Child of: production process
  • The material was exposed to react with its environment and meteoric water.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_f37a4790
  • Other Properties:

1.45.5 acid reaction

  • Child of: production process
  • The partial or complete dissolution of all parts of a material when exposed to acids.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_6237ab6b
  • Other Properties:

1.45.6 leaching

  • Child of: production process
  • The dissolution of specific parts of a material by covering or submerging it in a solution such as an acid, solvent, or water.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_5916e942
  • Other Properties:

1.45.7 grinding

  • Child of: production process
  • The material was mechanically reduced to smaller particles by applying friction.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_a1b2b905
  • Other Properties:

1.45.8 heating

  • Child of: production process
  • The material was exposed to high temperatures.
  • Concept URI: http://vocab.terralid.org#c_22488ba9
  • Other Properties:
